criticalLimit: Induction populations and Week-8 endpoint differ from BOTTOM maintenance Week-44 randomized responder-trial design; not independent maintenance replication.

criticalLimit: Complete hierarchy, multiplicity and independent patient-level validation are not available from this topline filing alone.

criticalLimit: Reported group sizes and stratification do not alone prove prospective power assumptions, final SAP adequacy or missing-data robustness.

evidence: On the 580-patient randomized double-blind ABTECT-Maintenance exact-trial Phase 3 readout, Week-44 clinical remission occurred in 98/193 (50.8%) at 25mg and 100/195 (51.3%) at 50mg versus 20/192 (10.4%) placebo. Sponsor reports stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 percentage points with both p<0.0001. Observed current results, not predictions.
criticalLimit: The readout is issuer-reported (SEC-filed), detailed prespecified effect confidence intervals, full SAP, ascertainment, and handling of missing data are not fully independently verified. Patients were induction responders re-randomized for maintenance; this is not efficacy in all initiating patients. Cross-program comparator is contextual only.

evidence: ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 initial induction responders (placebo 192, 25mg 193, 50mg 195), reporting Week-44 clinical remission 10.4%, 50.8% and 51.3% with stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 points, both p<0.0001; multiplicity and conservative missing-outcome scenarios are not supplied in full SEC summary.
criticalLimit: Reported p-values and predeclared stratification are not substitutes for accessible final SAP, confidence intervals for all contrasts, imputation, sensitivity analyses or an independently reanalysed dataset. Applicant-controlled topline is the source, so robustness is not fully established.

evidence: ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 induction responders across 25mg, 50mg and placebo and found Week-44 clinical remission near 51% in both doses versus 10.4% placebo. Sponsor also reports sustained clinical remission among Week-8 remission subgroups 67.1% and 65.6% vs 15.7% placebo. Separate prior induction trials demonstrated consistent 50mg benefit; 25mg induction was less consistent.
criticalLimit: Maintenance durability is measured in a selected responder population; the maintenance phase itself has no separate blinded confirmatory maintenance study in these sources. Induction and maintenance outcomes involve different populations/endpoints. Long-term 7-year extension described by sponsor is uncontrolled and not independent replication.

evidence: SEC-hosted ABTECT-Maintenance arm table (placebo n192, 25mg n193, 50mg n195): any TEAE 50.0%,58.0%,71.8%; serious TEAE 4.2%,2.6%,5.6%; study-drug discontinuations due to TEAE 6.8%,2.6%,4.6%; deaths 0 all groups. Serious/severe infection events reported 1.0%,1.0%,0.5%. Non-melanoma skin cancers 1 in placebo and 3 each in 25/50mg arms; single cases of prostate, breast and dysplasia in 50mg with attribution uncertain.
criticalLimit: Dose-related increase in any TEAE (50mg 71.8% vs placebo 50%) counters a uniformly favorable safety claim. Serious event counts are small and uncommon outcomes underpowered; trial selection limits generalizability. Attribution of skin cancers and longer exposure risk not established by topline.

evidence: Peer-reviewed ENERGIZE randomized NTD thalassemia trial: treatment-emergent events in 107/129 (83%) mitapivat vs 50/63 (79%) placebo. Headache occurred in 29/129 (22%) versus 6/63 (10%); initial insomnia 18/129 (14%) versus 3/63 (5%); nausea 15/129 (12%) versus 5/63 (8%); no deaths. Hemoglobin responders 42% versus 2%. Seven mitapivat and one placebo participants stopped study treatment before week 24; this is not specifically an adverse-event discontinuation count.
criticalLimit: The public abstract does not separately provide all arm-level serious-event and causality categories; the different thalassemia populations cannot be combined to claim head-to-head safety.

evidence: Conference abstract O33 with exact NCT04770753: 182 entered OLE, 121 continuing mitapivat, 61 crossover; among 55 original randomized responders mean Hb response duration 17.9 (SD3.6) weeks within double-blind period versus 43.6 (SD24.2) weeks cumulatively through OLE. Seventy-two of 121 (59.5%) originally active-treated achieved an OLE Hb response and some lasted up to 93.3 weeks.
criticalLimit: OLE lacked placebo comparator, enrollment selected DB completers, includes post-hoc responder classification, different follow-up exposure (median 71 weeks active-active vs 44 weeks placebo-active) and potential informative dropout. Longer period is encouraging for persistence but uncertain for causal replication.

evidence: ENERGIZE-T trial NCT04770779: treatment emergent AEs 155/172 (90%) mitapivat and 71/85 (84%) placebo; serious AEs 19/172 (11%) versus 13/85 (15%); ten (6%) vs one (1%) discontinued study treatment for adverse events. Open-label long-term safety remains ongoing.
criticalLimit: Reported 48-week randomized safety denominators; does not prove longer term safety or FDA benefit-risk acceptance.

evidence: 48-week double-blind ENERGIZE-T treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were 10/172 (6%) mitapivat versus 1/85 (1%) placebo; no deaths reported. OLE endpoints pending.
criticalLimit: Duration 48 weeks; adverse-event causality and longer term risk not independently settled.

evidence: ENERGIZE-T transfusion reduction 52/171 (30%) mitapivat versus 11/87 (13%) placebo; adjusted difference 18 points (95% CI 8–27), p=0.0003.
criticalLimit: Randomized 48-week result in transfusion-dependent adults; open-label extension is separate.

evidence: ENERGIZE-T NCT04770779 used a 48-week randomized blinded period and a primary transfusion response defined in any consecutive 12-week interval. Its extension is open-label and planned up to five years. The 48-week endpoint is not proof each patient maintained response across 48 weeks.
criticalLimit: Ongoing extension is not independent placebo-controlled replication; long-term individual response durability cannot be inferred from primary 12-week response window.

evidence: Peer-reviewed ENERGIZE-T TDT thalassemia trial: AEs in 155/172 (90%) mitapivat versus 71/85 (84%) placebo; SAEs 19/172 (11%) versus 13/85 (15%), and AE-driven treatment discontinuation 10/172 (6%) versus 1/85 (1%). No deaths. Transfusion reduction response 52/171 (30%) versus 11/87 (13%), adjusted difference 17.6 percentage points.
criticalLimit: Mismatched safety (172 vs 85) and efficacy denominators (171 vs 87) are preserved; source notes one mistakenly treated participant. Limited 48-week exposure, laboratory liver risk, and no long-term postmarketing safety.

evidence: In peer-reviewed randomized ENERGIZE-T, 238 of 258 (92%) randomized participants completed the double-blind period. At least one qualifying 12-week transfusion-reduction response occurred in 52/171 (30%) mitapivat vs 11/87 (13%) placebo; adjusted difference 18 percentage points (95% CI 8–27), p=0.0003. Its long open-label extension continues and cannot be used as blinded durability replication.
criticalLimit: The primary 'any 12-week window' response does not establish sustained reduction for each participant across the entire 48-week period. Longer-term observational extension participants are selected and receive no concurrent placebo; results, attrition patterns and long-horizon response trajectories remain incompletely disclosed.

{"eligibilityCriteria":"Inclusion Criteria:

* Signed and dated Institutional Review Board/Independent Ethics Committee-approved informed consent form prior to study-specific screening procedures.
* Confirmed histologic diagnosis of high-grade (Grade 3) serous, epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube carcinoma.
* Patients must have platinum-resistant disease (defined as RECIST v1.1 defined progression \<6 months from completion of a platinum-containing therapy).
* Must consent to provide archival tumor-tissue block or slides. Patients may consent to an optional tumor biopsy if archival tumor is unavailable.
* Has a life expectancy of ≥3 months.
* At least one lesion that meets the definition of measurable disease by RECIST v1.1
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0 or 1.
* Able to comply with protocol requirements.
* Able to swallow and retain oral medication and does not have uncontrolled emesis.
* Received at least 1 but ≤3 lines of prior systemic anticancer therapy and at least 1 prior line of platinum therapy and prior treatment with bevacizumab is required.
* Has adequate organ function meeting the following laboratory-test criteria: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥1500 cells/mm\^3, Platelet count ≥100,000/mm\^3, Hemoglobin ≥9 g/dL, Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤2.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN), or ≤5 × ULN in context of liver metastases, Total bilirubin ≤1.5 × ULN, and Albumin ≥3 g/dL, and creatinine clearance \>40 mL/min/1.73 m\^2 (measured or estimated).
* Negative pregnancy test for patients of childbearing potential; patients of childbearing potential must agree to use highly effective contraceptive method(s); hormonal contraceptives are not allowed.
* Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) approved vaccines are accepted concomitant medications when recommended by the Investigator.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Has clinically relevant toxicity from prior systemic anticancer therapies or radiotherapy that has not resolved to ≤Grade 1 prior to randomization.
* Has had any major surgery within 4 weeks prior to randomization.
* Has low-grade endometrioid, clear cell, mucinous, or sarcomatous histology, or mixed tumors containing any of these histologies, or low-grade or borderline ovarian tumor.
* Has primary platinum-refractory disease, defined as disease that did not respond to or has progressed ≤1 month of the last dose of first-line platinum-containing chemotherapy.
* Has not received prior bevacizumab treatment.
* Has been treated with the following prior to randomization: chemotherapy, immunotherapy, investigational agent treatments for disease under study within 28 days before first dose of study drug, radiotherapy not completed at least 2 weeks prior to first dose of study drug, hormonal anticancer therapies within 7 days of first dose of study drug, and systemic, inhaled, or prescription strength topical corticosteroids within 21 days of first dose of study drug.

* Has toxicities of prior therapies that have not resolved by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI-CTCAE) v5.0, ≤Grade 1.
* Requires treatment with chronic or frequently used oral corticosteroids for medical conditions or illnesses.
* Has a history of severe hypersensitivity or severe reaction to any of the study drugs.
* Is receiving concurrent treatment with mifepristone or other glucocorticoid receptor (GR) modulators.
* Has peripheral neuropathy from any cause \>Grade 1.
* Pregnant or lactating patients or patients expecting to conceive children within the projected duration of the trial, starting with the screening visit through at least 1 month after the last dose of relacorilant, or 6 months after the last dose of nab-paclitaxel whichever is the longest.
* Has clinically significant uncontrolled condition(s) or condition which, in the opinion of the Investigator, may confound the results of the trial or interfere with the patient's safety or participation.
* Has current chronic/active infection with human immunodeficiency virus or current chronic/active infection with hepatitis C virus or hepatitis B virus.
* Has any untreated or symptomatic central nervous system (CNS) metastases.
* Patients with a history of other malignancy within 3 years prior to randomization.
* Is taking a concomitant medication that is a strong cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A inhibitor or strong CYP3A inducer, or that is a substrate of CYP3A with a narrow therapeutic window.
* Concurrent treatment on other investigational treatment studies for the treatment of ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer.

{"eligibilityCriteria":"Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subject must be ≥18 years of age, at the time of signing the informed consent (≥20 in Japan).
2. A serum anti-GM-CSF autoantibody test result confirming autoimmune PAP.
3. History of PAP, based on examination of a lung biopsy, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) cytology, or a high-resolution computed tomogram (HRCT) of the chest.
4. A diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide of 70% predicted or lower adjusted for hemoglobin (%DLCOadj) at the screening and baseline visits.
5. Change in %DLCO adj of \<15% points during the screening period.
6. Demonstrated functional impairment in the treadmill exercise test (defined as a peak metabolic equivalent (MET) ≤8).
7. Willing and able to come off supplemental oxygen use prior to and during the treadmill exercise test, the DLCO assessment, and the arterial blood gas sampling.
8. Resting oxygen saturation (SpO2) \>85% during 15 minutes without use of supplemental oxygen at the screening visits.
